article.summary: RIYADH: Saudi civil defence sent an all-clear on Saturday after issuing alerts for a second time for potential danger in Riyadh and the city of Al-Kharj east of the capital, amid an uptick in attacks by Houthis on the Gulf country.The alerts were the first for the capital since Houthis in neighbouring Yemen intensified their attacks on Saudi Arabia.AReutersjournalist heard two booms in Riyadh’s Olaya area.The alerts come hours after the Houthis’ spokesperson said the group had foiled unspecified “criminal attempts” in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, blaming Saudi Arabia and vowing a response.There was no immediate comment from the Saudi government’s media office on the Houthis’ statement.The Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, have been launching attacks towards Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade against Riyadh in July, with strikes targeting Saudi vessels in the Red Sea.One killed as Saudi Arabia intercepts drone launched by Yemen’s Hou...

article.title: Saudi Arabia to halt crude supplies to European refiners in October
article.summary: Saudi Arabia to halt crude supplies to European refiners in OctoberSaudi Arabia’s state oil company Aramco has told at least some European refiners that they will receive no Saudi crude next month following the shutdown of the kingdom’s East-West oil pipeline, Bloomberg reported.The disruption follows attacks that damaged three pumping stations along the 1,200km East-West pipeline, which had been carrying about 4 million to 5 million barrels of crude a day to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.Earlier today, reports said that King Fahd Port in Yanbu was targeted by Houthi ballistic missiles.European OECD countries were importing about 577,000 barrels per day from Saudi Arabia as of June, according to International Energy Agency data cited by Bloomberg.Saudi Arabia has been seeking alternative routes, including increased shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, while repairs to the pipeline are expected to take weeks.
